verses.text: Solomon decided to build a house in honor of the LORD's name and a palace for his kingdom.
He assigned seventy thousand men to haul materials, eighty thousand to cut stone in the mountains, and thirty-six hundred to supervise them.
Solomon sent this message to King Huram of Tyre: "Please do for me what you did for my father David when you sent him cedar to build a house to live in.

I'm about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God and dedicate it to him. We'll burn fragrant incense before him, keep the sacred bread on display, and present burnt offerings morning and evening, on Sabbaths, at new moons, and at the appointed festivals of the LORD our God. This is a lasting requirement for Israel.
The house I'm building will be great because our God is greater than all gods.
But who could build a house that holds him when even the highest heavens can't contain him? Who am I to build him a house except as a place to burn incense before him?

Send me someone skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, and purple, crimson, and blue fabric, who also knows how to engrave. He'll work with the skilled craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem whom my father David provided.
Send me cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon as well. I know your workers know how to cut timber there. My workers will work alongside yours
to prepare plenty of timber for me, because the house I'm about to build will be great and wonderful.
I'll give your woodcutters twenty thousand cors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand baths of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
King Huram of Tyre sent Solomon a written reply: "The LORD made you king because he loves his people."

Huram went on, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth. He gave King David a wise son with good judgment and understanding who will build a house for the LORD and a palace for his kingdom.
I'm sending Huram-abi, a skilled craftsman with good understanding.

His mother is from the tribe of Dan and his father is from Tyre. He can work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, purple and blue fabric, fine linen, and crimson fabric. He can do any kind of engraving and work out any design. Give him a place among your craftsmen and those who served my lord David, your father.
Please send your workers the wheat, barley, oil, and wine you mentioned.
We'll cut as much timber from Lebanon as you need and float it by sea on rafts to Joppa. You can take it up from there to Jerusalem."
Solomon counted all the foreigners living in Israel, following the census his father David had taken. They numbered a hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
He assigned seventy thousand to haul materials, eighty thousand to cut stone in the mountains, and thirty-six hundred supervisors to assign the people their work.
